questions.question: Which of the following classifications do humans NOT fall under?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Porifera**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Humans are classified as animals by Carolus Linnaeus (called the father of taxonomy)** and are termed the scientific name homo sapiens in 1758.
 
• Humans are classified based on the groups **Animalia (Kingdom), Chordata (Phylum), Vertebrata (Subphylum), Mammalia (Class), Primates (Order), Hominidae (Superfamily), and Homo (Genus).**
 
• **Porifera are sponges that are invertebrate animals that live in aquatic habitat** and is not one of the human classifications. **Hence option 2 is correct.**
 
 
• These are made of a group of cells that work together for functioning.
 
• They live in marine, and freshwater lakes as well as shallow ocean conditions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Species with phylum Chordata (animals with a backbone) are vertebrates and humans have a backbone and so they belong to the animal phylum called Chordates.**
 
• Humans resemble apes because of the bodies that are structurally and genetically close to apes and so humans belong to the family Hominidae.
 
 
• **Hominidae refers to the family of humans and extinct or close relatives**.
 
 
 
• **Vertebrata is a subphylum under phylum Chordata** and vertebrates refer to the animals that** have back bone and the skeleton.**

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct?

I. The nutrition requirements of adolescents are higher than adults.

II. Adolescents are generally grouped in the age group of 10 to 19 years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Adolescents need more nutrients than adults **because they gain at least 40 per cent of their adult weight and 15 per cent of their adult height during this period.
 
• Inadequate intake can lead to delayed sexual development and slower linear growth.
 
 
• **Hence Statement 1 is correct.**
 
 
 
• Adolescents are generally grouped in the age group** of 10 to 19 years. **
 
 
• **Hence Statement 2 is correct.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Adolescence **is characterized by rapid physical, social, mental, and emotional changes.
 
• It is also a time of opportunity and risk. In the view of Stanley Hall (the father of adolescent psychology), it’s a time of “storm and stress.”
 
 
• Adolescence is a period of rapid growth when young people acquire new abilities and face new challenges, in this stage children are in conflict with their parents, are moody, and tend to spend more time with their peers.
 
• It is the transitional stage of childhood and adulthood when a child develops physically and psychologically into an adult.
 
• Adolescents fail to think clearly, creating great frustration and stress in their lives.
 
• It is also known as the problem age because rapid physical growth leaves teenagers feeling awkward, self-conscious, uncoordinated, embarrassed, and even confused.

questions.question: Amoeba acquires its food through the process of ______.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Amoebas** acquire their food through the process of **phagocytosis**, which involves extending their **pseudopodia (temporary protrusions of the cell membrane)** around a **food particle** and then engulfing it into their **cytoplasm. **
 
• Once inside the cell, the **food particle** is enclosed in a **food vacuole**, which then **fuses** with lysosomes for digestion.</str

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of calcium in our body?

options.text: It plays an important role in blood clotting.
It is associated with healthy bones and teeth

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It helps the digestive system**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Calcium is the most abundant mineral in the human body and has many important functions,** accounting for 1.5 to 2% of total body weight.**
 
• About 1,200 grams of calcium are present in the body of an adult human;** more than 99% of that amount is found in bones.**
 
• Most of the body's calcium is stored in the bones and teeth, which serves to support their structure.
 
• Recommendations for calcium are provided in the** Dietary Reference Intake, developed by Medical Institute of the National Academy of Sciences.**
 
• It consists of **calcium hydroxide, calcium carbonate, calcium fluoride, calcium phosphate, and citrate.**
 
• **Parathyroid hormone controls the amount of calcium.**
 
• Although calcium is a very important component in bone and is found in large quantities, increased salt or sodium intake leads to bone weakening leading to a decrease in the calcium content of the bone resulting in osteoporosis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Nutrients types: 
 
• Macro-nutrients: nutrients that we need in huge amounts in our bodies.
 
 
• Carbohydrate
 
• Fat
 
• Protein
 
• Water
 
 
 
• Micro-nutrients: nutrients that we need in smaller amounts.
 
 
• Vitamins
 
• Minerals
 
• Dietary fiber.
 
 
 
• The energy value of food is measured in heating units called calories or Killo calories.
 
• A kilocalorie is equal to 1000 calories.
 
• 57% carbs, 30% fats, and 13% protein, is our body's requirement. 
 
• Basic energy requirement:
 
 
• For every kg of body weight, 1.3 calories of energy are required every hour.
 
 
 
• Extra energy requirement:

questions.question: The strongest muscle (based on its weight) of the body is the masseter muscle and is located in the:
questions.solution:
**The strongest muscle (based on its weight)** of the body is the** masseter muscle **and is located in the **__jaw__**.

 
• **The muscle masseter** is a** facial muscle **that plays a major role in the chewing of solid foods.
 
• It is a facial muscle that plays a major role in the chewing of solid foods. The muscle has a parallelogram-like shape, binding to the** mandible (lower jawbone) and the cheekbone.**
 
• The muscle's function during the entire muscle's bilateral contraction is to lift the mandible and raise the lower jaw. The elevation of the mandible happens when the jaws are closed.
 
• **The masseter muscle **is the most evident muscle of mastication since it is the most superficial and one of the strongest.

questions.question: The yolk of an egg contains more than 90% of which of the given vitamins?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin B12.**__

__
 
• The yolk of an egg contains more than 90% **Vitamin B12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vitamin B12** is a nutrient that helps keep the **body's nerve and blood cells healthy and helps make DNA, **the genetic material in all cells.
 
• It also helps prevent a type of anemia called** megaloblastic anemia** that makes people tired and weak.
 
• It is mainly found in animal products, especially meat and dairy products.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Vitamin C:**

 
 
• Vitamin C is a **water-soluble vitami**n that’s found in many foods, particularly fruits and vegetables.
 
• Deficiency symptoms include **bleeding gums, frequent bruising and infections, poor wound healing, anemia, and scurvy.**
 
 
 
• ** Vitamin K:**
 
 
• Vitamin K refers to a group of **fat-soluble vitamins** that play a role in **blood clotting, bone metabolism, and regulating blood calcium levels**.
 
• Sources include meat, dairy products, eggs, and Japanese “natto,” made from fermented soybeans.
 
 
 
• **Vitamin A:**
 
 
• Vitamin A is a **fat-soluble vitamin** that is naturally present in many foods.
 
• Vitamin A is important for **normal vision, the immune system, and reproduction.**
 
• Vitamin A also helps the** heart, lungs, kidneys, and other organs work properly.**

questions.question: What is the specific field of study focused on examining extinct animals?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Paleontology**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Paleontology** is the specific field of study that focuses on the examination of **extinct animals** and other organisms through their fossil remains.
 
• It involves the study of **fossils**, which include preserved remains, impressions, or traces of organisms from the past.
 
• Paleontology bridges the fields of **biology** and **geology** to understand the evolutionary history of life on Earth.
 
• Key tools in paleontology include techniques from **stratigraphy, radiometric dating, and comparative anatomy**.
 
• Paleontologists study extinct species to gain insights into **evolutionary processes, environmental changes, and extinction events.**
 
• It includes specialized subfields such as **vertebrate paleontology** (focused on animals with backbones) and **invertebrate paleontology** (focused on animals without backbones).
 
• Paleontology contributes to understanding phenomena such as the extinction of **dinosaurs** and the emergence of **mammals.**
 
• Famous discoveries in paleontology include fossils of **Tyrannosaurus rex, Archaeopteryx**, and early hominids like **Australopithecus.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gerontology**__

 __
 
• **Gerontology** is the study of aging and older adults, focusing on biological, psychological, and social aspects.
 
• It aims to improve the quality of life and well-being of the elderly through research and practical applications.
 
• Gerontology often overlaps with medical fields such as **geriatrics**, which deals with healthcare for the elderly.
 
 
 
• **Economic Geology**__
 __
 
• **Economic geology** focuses on the study of materials that can be used for economic and industrial purposes, such as **minerals, fossil fuels, and metals.**
 
• It examines the processes of formation, location, extraction, and utilization of **natural resources.**
 
• This field is crucial for understanding and managing **mining operations and energy resources.**
 
 
 
• **Glaciology**__
 
 
• **Glaciology** is the study of glaciers, ice sheets, and other forms of ice in the natural environment.
 
• It focuses on the processes of **ice formation, movement, and melting.**
 
• Glaciology plays a vital role in understanding **climate change** and its impact on sea levels and ecosystems.

• **Carbohydrates**

questions.question: In ruminants like cattle, bacteria present in ________ helps in digestion of cellulose.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**rumen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In ruminants like cattle, bacteria present in the rumen (the largest compartment of the stomach) play a crucial role in the digestion of cellulose.
 
• The rumen is a fermentation chamber where complex carbohydrates, such as cellulose from plant material, are broken down by microbial fermentation.
 
• Bacteria in the rumen possess cellulolytic enzymes that break down cellulose into simpler forms that can be further digested and utilized by the ruminant host.
 
• This symbiotic relationship between ruminants and rumen bacteria allows them to efficiently extract nutrients from plant-based diets.
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3c75e2c157479fe2a43748fcd07a27548b2d9a6f8bfacd85ce738d3d249751e6.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: How many balanced meals of average size each day should adolescents have?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nutrition:**

 
 
• **​**Adolescents are in a** stage of rapid growth and development.**
 
• **They need balanced and nutritious meals to support this growth.**
 
• Three balanced meals a day can help provide the necessary **nutrients, vitamins, and minerals.**
 
 
 
• **Energy Levels:**
 
 
• **​**Eating three meals a day helps maintain energy levels throughout the day.
 
• This is important as adolescents often** engage in many activities, including school, sports, and hobbies.**
 
 
 
• **Health:**
 
 
• **​**Regular meals contribute to **overall health.**
 
• Skipping meals can lead to** overeating later in the day or choosing fast food and snacks that are not as nutritious.**
 
 
 
• **Habits:**
 
 
• **​**Establishing the habit of having **three meals a day can help adolescents learn about portion sizes and make healthier food choices.**
 
• This habit can also contribute to a balanced diet.
 
 
 
• **Hunger Management:**
 
 
• **​**Eating three meals a day can **help manage hunger levels and prevent overeating or binge eating.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Additional Info about Adolescents:**

 
 
• Adolescence is a transitional stage of **physical and psychological development that generally occurs during the period from puberty to legal adulthood.**
 
• It's a critical period of** growth and development, so proper nutrition is crucial.**
 
• Adolescents require a** higher intake of energy and nutrients compared** to adults because they are growing and developing rapidly.
 
• This includes not only** physical growth but also cognitive development.**
 
• Regular exercise and a **balanced diet can help ensure healthy development during these years.**

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about nutrients are correct?

Statement A: C, H, O, N, P and K are macro nutrients.

Statement B: Fe, Mn, Ni, Co and Mo are micronutrients.

Statement C: Micronutrients are not essential for our body.

options.text: All statements A, B and C

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only statements A and B**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Macro nutrients** include elements such as Carbon (C), Hydrogen (H), Oxygen (O), Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), and Potassium (K).
 
• **Micro nutrients** include elements like Iron (Fe), Manganese (Mn), Nickel (Ni), Cobalt (Co), and Molybdenum (Mo).
 
• Both macro and micronutrients are essential for plant growth and human health, though required in different quantities.
 
• Statement C is incorrect because micronutrients, despite being needed in smaller amounts, are essential for various bodily functions and overall health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Macronutrients:** These are nutrients required in larger amounts and include carbohydrates, proteins, and fats, along with elements like C, H, O, N, P, and K.
 
• **Micronutrients:** These are nutrients required in smaller amounts but are crucial for various physiological functions. Examples include vitamins and minerals like Fe, Mn, Ni, Co, and Mo.
 
• **Essential Nutrients:** Both macro and micronutrients are categorized as essential because the body cannot synthesize them in sufficient amounts.
 
• **Role of Micronutrients:** Micronutrients play vital roles in enzyme function, hormone production, and maintaining the immune system.
 
• **Deficiency Impacts:** Deficiency of micronutrients can lead to various health issues, including anemia (iron deficiency), scurvy (vitamin C deficiency), and osteoporosis (calcium deficiency).

questions.question: Which body part of fishes helps them to change directions and keep their body balance in water?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Fins and tail**__** **(also known as the caudal fin) are the locomotive organs in fishes as their movement helps the fishes to move, maintain balance and change directions underwater.
 
• They may be bony, cartilaginous or fibrous in nature.
 
• Fish have **scales** to protect the skin of the fish from attacks from predators, parasites and other injuries.
 
• **Fish gills** are organs that allow fish to breathe underwater. Most fish exchange gases like oxygen and carbon dioxide using gills that are protected under gill covers on both sides of the pharynx (throat).

questions.question: Which is the most important protein component in milk, both quantitatively and nutritionally, that accounts for about 80% of the total protein in bovine milk?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Casein**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Casein** is the most abundant protein in milk, making up about 80% of the total protein content in bovine milk.
 
• It is nutritionally valuable due to its high quality and rich composition of essential amino acids.
 
• Casein proteins are slow-digesting, providing a sustained release of amino acids into the bloodstream.
 
• It plays an important role in providing the necessary nutrients for the growth and development of young mammals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Actin**

 
 
• Actin is a protein that forms microfilaments and is involved in various types of cell motility and structure.
 
• It is not a major component of milk but is essential in muscle contraction and cellular movements.
 
 
 
• **Albumin**
 
 
• Albumin is a type of protein found in blood plasma, egg white, and milk.
 
• While it is present in milk, it does not constitute the majority of milk proteins.
 
• It is important for maintaining the osmotic pressure necessary for proper distribution of body fluids between body tissues and the bloodstream.
 
 
 
• **Pepsin**
 
 
• Pepsin is a digestive enzyme that breaks down proteins into peptides.
 
• It is produced in the stomach and is not a component of milk.
 
• It functions in the digestive system to help in the digestion of proteins from food.
 
 
 
• **Casein**
 
 
• Casein is a family of related phosphoproteins that are commonly found in mammalian milk.
 
• It forms a gel or clot in the stomach, which makes it very efficient in nutrient supply.
 
• Casein is used in cheese-making and as a food additive for its binding properties.
 
• Its ability to provide a slow and sustained release of amino acids makes it highly beneficial for muscle repair and growth.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

Saliva contains an enzyme called salivary lipase that breaks down starch into simple sugar
Food enters the stomach through the oesophagus (esophagus)

questions.solution:

__

• An enzyme called **amylase **in saliva breaks down** starches (complex carbohydrates) into sugars,** which your body can more easily absorb.
 
• Saliva also contains an enzyme called lingual lipase, which breaks down fats.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b905d7003d06f4639a74ccbd24f9cf2bdcff2761f7ec676a8d5b9d6de2e57d19.png]

 Nutrients

 Fats
 Fat digestion happens when reaches the small intestine (Duodenum).
 
 

 Proteins

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Invertebrates do not possess a backbone or an internal skeleton.
 
• They exhibit either radial or bilateral body symmetry.
 
• They have a pair of solid nerve cords, situated ventrally and bearing segmentally arranged ganglia.
 
• They typically have an open circulatory system as there is no organization in the distribution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Invertebrates constitute a vast majority of animal species on Earth, covering groups such as insects, arachnids, mollusks, crustaceans, and more.
 
• Despite lacking a backbone, many invertebrates have specialized adaptations that allow them to thrive in diverse environments.
 
• The study of invertebrates is crucial for understanding ecological interactions, evolutionary biology, and the development of medical and technological innovations.
 
• Invertebrates play key roles in ecosystems, including pollination, decomposition, and serving as food for other animals.

questions.question: Adipose tissue is a type of ______ tissue in the human body.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**connective**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Adipose tissue** is a type of loose **connective tissue** located mainly beneath the skin.
 
• The cells of this tissue are specialized to **store fats.**
 
• Connective tissues are most abundant and widely distributed in the body of complex animals.
 
• They are named connective tissues because of their special function of linking and supporting other tissues/organs of the body.
 
• They range from soft connective tissues to specialized types, which include cartilage, bone, adipose, and blood.
 
• In all connective tissues except blood, the cells secrete fibres of structural proteins called collagen or elastin.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Epithelial tissue:

 
 
• The epithelial tissues are formed by cells that cover the organ surface such as the surface of the skin, the airways, the reproductive tract, and the inner lining of the digestive tract.
 
 
 
• Muscular tissues:
 
 
• Muscular tissue is a soft tissue that composes muscles.
 
• Skeletal muscle (voluntary muscles), cardiac muscle (involuntary muscles) are examples of it.
 
 
 
• Nervous tissue:
 
 
• The main components of the nervous system are the brain, spinal cord, and nerves which regulate and control body functions.
 
• It is made up of neurons that have important functions in the nervous system.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of permanent tissue?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Intercellular spaces are present.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The characteristic features of permanent tissue are:
 
 
• **Cells have intercellular spaces to keep them separated.**
 
• The cells may be living or dead, i.e.the protoplasm is either present or absent.
 
• Tissue may have only one type of cell or may have different kinds of cells.
 
• The cell wall is either cellulosic or along with cellulose other complex carbohydrates may be present.
 
• Cells may** vary in shape, **i.e., either** round or oval or polygonal, **etc.
 
• In the living cells, the cytoplasm is present surrounding** a large central vacuole.**
 
• **Cells do not divide at all.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of permanent tissue: **
 
• **Permanent tissues are of three types, namely –**
 
 
• **(a) Simple tissue, (b) Complex tissue and (c) Secretory tissue.**
 
 
 
• **​Simple permanent tissue**
 
 
• Simple permanent tissue is composed of a single type of cells that have comparable origin, structure, and function.
 
 
 
• **Types of simple permanent tissue**
 
 
• **Parenchyma** – It provides temporary support and maintains the shape of the plant body. They have thin-walled cells with large vacuoles.
 
• **Collenchyma** – It provides mechanical support and elasticity and flexibility to young dicotyledonous plants. They have thickened cell walls at corners, giving mechanical strength.
 
• **Sclerenchyma **– It provides strength and toughness to plant parts. They have dead cells with extremely thick walls (lignin deposition). Sclerenchyma may be either fibres or sclereids
 
 
 
• **Complex permanent tissue**
 
 
• Complex permanent tissue is composed of two or more two types of cells and contributes to a general function.
 
• They organize together to carry out similar particular functions in the plant body.
 
• It is also known as vascular tissue.
 
 
 
• **Types of complex tissue:**
 
 
• **Xylem **– The xylem tissue is accountable for the transmission of water and minerals from the roots to the leaves and stems.
 
• **Phloem** – This complex permanent tissue helps in the translocation of food that is prepared by photosynthesis in the leaves to diverse parts of the plant.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the notochord in chordates?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Support**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **notochord** is a flexible, rod-shaped structure that provides **support** to the body of chordates, especially during their embryonic stage.
 
• It forms the primary axis of the body and acts as a **scaffold** for the development of the vertebral column in vertebrates.
 
• The notochord is located between the digestive tube and the nerve cord and is composed of **cells derived from the mesoderm**.
 
• In most vertebrates, the notochord is replaced by the vertebral column during development, but it still plays a crucial role in **body structure and organization** during early embryogenesis.
 
• The presence of a notochord is one of the primary characteristics of the **phylum Chordata**, which includes all vertebrates, cephalochordates, and urochordates.
 
• In species like **amphioxus (lancelets)**, the notochord persists throughout life, providing continuous support and structural integrity.
 
• The notochord is also significant for inducing the development of the **neural tube**, which later forms the central nervous system, including the brain and spinal cord.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Locomotion**__

 __
 
• While the notochord provides structural **support**, it does not directly aid in **locomotion**. Instead, locomotion in chordates is facilitated by structures like **muscles and fins** or limbs.
 
• In some aquatic chordates, the notochord works in conjunction with muscles to allow a wave-like motion for **propulsion**.
 
 
 
• **Digestion**__
 __
 
• The notochord is not involved in the process of **digestion**. Digestion is carried out by the **digestive system**, which includes organs like the stomach, intestine, and associated glands.
 
• The digestive tube in chordates lies **below the notochord**.
 
 
 
• **Respiration**__
 
 
• Respiration in chordates is facilitated by specialized structures like **gills, lungs, or skin**, depending on the species and their habitat.
 
• The notochord does not play a role in **gas exchange** or respiration.

questions.question: Which of the following characteristics was used by Aristotle to classify animals?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Habitat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Aristotle, known as the **"Father of Zoology"**, was one of the first scientists to classify animals systematically.
 
• He used the **habitat** of animals as a primary criterion for classification.
 
• According to Aristotle, animals could be grouped based on where they lived, such as in water, air, or on land.
 
• This classification system led to three broad groups:
 
 
• **Aquatic animals:** Animals that live in water, such as fish and whales.
 
• **Terrestrial animals:** Animals that live on land, such as lions and elephants.
 
• **Aerial animals:** Animals that live in the air, such as birds and bats.
 
 
 
• This system was a foundational concept in the study of zoology and helped in understanding the diversity of life forms.
 
• Although this method is now outdated, it laid the groundwork for modern biological classification systems, such as the Linnaean taxonomy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Specialised organs**__

 __
 
• Specialized organs refer to body parts adapted for specific functions, such as the heart for pumping blood or lungs for respiration.
 
• While Aristotle noted some anatomical differences, his primary classification was not based on the presence or absence of specialized organs.
 
• Modern taxonomy, however, does consider organ specialization in classifying species.
 
 
 
• **Types of body cells**__
 __
 
• The differentiation of body cells, such as prokaryotic vs. eukaryotic cells, was not a concept known during Aristotle's time.
 
• This characteristic became relevant only after the discovery of the cell by **Robert Hooke** in the 17th century.
 
 
 
• **Photosynthesis**__
 
 
• Photosynthesis is a process by which plants convert sunlight into energy.
 
• Since Aristotle focused on animals, photosynthesis was irrelevant to his classification system.
 
• However, this process plays a crucial role in the classification of plants in modern botany.

questions.question: Who among the following introduced binominal nomenclature of biological classification?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Linnaeus**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Carolus Linnaeus **introduced binomial nomenclature, the modern system of naming organisms, in the 1750s.
 
• Linnaeus is** also known as the "father of modern taxonomy"**
 
• Linnaeus was a **Swedish biologist and physician **who was born in Råshult, Sweden in 1707.
 
• Linnaeus **classified organisms into two kingdoms: Plantae and Animalia.**
 
• He **used a variety of criteria for classification, including cell wall, locomotion, mode of nutrition, and response to external stimuli.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aristotle****​**

 
 
• Aristotle is often considered the **father of biology** due to his extensive work in **natural history** and his systematic study of living organisms.
 
• He made detailed observations of plants and animals, classifying them into **two broad groups**: **animals** and **plants**.
 
• He also introduced the concept of **empirical observation** and **classification** of species based on their characteristics.
 
• **Aristotle's classification system** was based on physical traits and behaviour.
 
• He proposed a **ladder of life** where organisms were organized from simpler forms to more complex ones.
 
• His works laid the foundation for **taxonomy** and **ecology**, though many of his ideas were later revised or replaced by more modern scientific theories.
 
 
 
• **John Ray**
 
 
• **​**John Ray was an English naturalist who is considered one of the **founders of modern biology and taxonomy.**
 
• Ray’s work was instrumental in the development of the **scientific classification of plants and animals.**
 
• He made a distinction between **species and varieties** and recognized the importance of r**eproductive isolation in maintaining species.**
 
• In his landmark work, Historia Plantarum (1686), Ray classified plants into **families and genera, and established a foundation for later plant classification systems.**
 
• He was also one of the first to define the concept of species as a group of organisms capable of interbreeding and producing fertile offspring.​
 
 
 
• **Charles Darwin **
 
 
• **​**Charles Darwin is** best known for his groundbreaking work on the theory of evolution**.
 
• His theory posited that species evolve over time through the process of natural selection, where traits that are advantageous for survival are more likely to be passed on to future generations.
 
• His **seminal book, On the Origin of Species (1859),** proposed that all species of life have descended from common ancestors and that the process of natural selection drives the diversity of life.
 
• Darwin’s work fundamentally changed the way scientists understood the origin of species and their adaptation to the environment.
 
• His **ideas laid the foundation for modern evolutionary biology and helped explain the diversity of life on Earth.**
 
• Darwin’s theory also influenced various fields, including g**enetics, paleontology, and ethology (study of animal behavior).**​

questions.question: If the Glycemic Index (GI) of a specific food is from 70 to 100, then the type of that food is:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**High-GI food**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Glycemic Index (GI)** is a numerical scale that measures how quickly a carbohydrate-containing food raises blood glucose levels after consumption.
 
• Foods are generally classified into three categories based on their GI values: **Low-GI**, **Medium-GI**, and **High-GI**.
 
• Foods with a GI value between **70 to 100** fall under the category of **High-GI foods**.
 
• High-GI foods cause a rapid spike in blood sugar levels because their carbohydrates are digested and absorbed quickly.
 
• Examples of High-GI foods include processed foods like **white bread**, **instant rice**, and **sugary beverages**.
 
• High-GI foods are beneficial in situations where quick energy is needed, such as during or after high-intensity exercise, but they are generally not recommended for people with conditions like **diabetes**.
 
• Understanding the GI of foods is crucial for maintaining healthy blood sugar levels and making informed dietary choices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Low-GI food**__

 __
 
• Low-GI foods have a GI value of **55 or less**.
 
• They cause a slow and steady increase in blood sugar levels and are ideal for people with **diabetes** or those looking to control their weight.
 
• Examples include **lentils**, **whole oats**, and **most fruits**.
 
 
 
• **Medium-GI food**__
 __
 
• Medium-GI foods have a GI value between **56 and 69**.
 
• These foods have a moderate impact on blood sugar levels and are considered a balanced option for energy.
 
• Examples include **brown rice**, **sweet potatoes**, and **whole wheat bread**.
 
 
 
• **Extremely low-GI food**__
 
 
• Foods with an extremely low GI value are generally rare and have a GI much lower than **55**.
 
• Examples may include foods that are non-carbohydrate-based, such as **meat**, **fish**, and **eggs**, which do not significantly affect blood sugar levels.

questions.question: Name a reproductive strategy in which parasites take advantage of the care of other individuals of the same species or different species to raise their young.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brood parasitism.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Brood parasitism:-**

 
 
• It is a **reproductive strategy **in which a **parasite lays its eggs** in the nest of **another individual **of the same species or different species, and the **host raises the parasite's young.**
 
• This strategy is often used by** birds**, such as cuckoos, cowbirds, and honeyguides, but it can also be observed in** insects, fish, and mammals.**
 
• Brood parasites have evolved various adaptations to increase their chances of success, such as** mimicking the appearance and behavior** of the host's eggs or chicks, laying their eggs at the same time as the host, or removing the host's eggs.
 
• Brood parasitism can have both** costs and benefits** for the host, depending on the **degree of similarity** between the **parasite and the host**, the number of parasites in the host's nest, and the availability of alternative nesting sites.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sexual parasitism:-**

 
 
• It also known as** mate parasitism**, refers to a reproductive strategy in which a** male or female gains access** to a mate or a nest by **deceiving or coercing the other individual. **
 
 
 
• **Klepto parasitism, or kleptoparasitism:-**
 
 
• It​** **refers to a feeding strategy in which a parasite steals food from another individual, often by chasing or harassing it.
 
 
 
• **Competitive parasitism, or social parasitism:-**
 
 
• It** **refers to a reproductive strategy in which a parasite takes over the resources and/or reproduction of a host, often by manipulating its behavior or physiology.

questions.question: In which of the following type of organism autotrophic nutrition is found?

• Some types of **bacteria are autotrophs.**

Mode of** Nutrition:**

questions.question: Which of the following is another name for starch found mainly in the pulp of seeds, fruits, tubers, roots and stems of plants, especially in corn, potatoes, wheat and rice?
questions.solution:

questions.question: What are the three parts of bacterial flagellum?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Filament, hook and basal body**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bacterium Flagella

 
 
• Bacterial flagella are made of the protein flagellin and are a coiled, thread-like structure with a sharp bend and a rotary motor at the base.
 
• It gives bacteria the ability to swim freely through a binary compound of aqueous, also known as motility or self-propulsion.
 
• It is composed of three major structural elements;
 
 
• Basal body
 
 
• It is joined to the cytoplasmic membrane and cell membrane.

 It is made up of rings that are surrounded by MotB proteins.
 
 
 
• Hook
 
 
• A hook is a name for the wider area at the base of the flagellum.
 
• It connects the filament to the base's motor protein.
 
 
 
• Filament
 
 
• It is a thin, hair-like structure emerging from the hook.
 
 
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://images.ctfassets.net/vrrt8fsfwf0e/1wAOVui8utRyH09gVA619H/00cdcf173ccf0e1c5989e57dcb705d44/Bacterial_Flagella_art_1.svg]

• The long, helical filament of bacterial flagella is made up of several flagellin subunits organised in a variety of tangled chains.
 
• A flagellum is made up of numerous parts and rotates, similar to a boat motor's propeller.
 
• Depending on the species, the diameter of bacterial flagella varies, which lies between 15 and 20 nm.
 
• Functions of Bacterial Flagella
 
 
• Role in pathogenesis
 
• Organ of locomotion
 
• Role in identification of organism

questions.question:
Anorexia Nervosa is an eating disorder characterised by ________.

 a) an abnormally heavy body weight

 b) an intense fear of losing weight

 c) a distorted perception of weight

 d) trying to lose weight by exercising excessively
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**c and d**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Anorexia Nervosa is characterized by a **distorted perception of weight** and body image, where individuals see themselves as overweight despite being underweight.
 
• Individuals with Anorexia Nervosa often engage in **excessive exercise, extreme dieting, and other behaviors to lose weight**.
 
• This disorder involves an **intense fear of gaining weight** and a persistent behavior to avoid weight gain.
 
• People suffering from this condition may have a **low body mass index (BMI)** due to restricted food intake.
 
• Anorexia Nervosa can lead to severe health complications, including **malnutrition, bone loss, and heart problems**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eating Disorders:** A range of psychological disorders characterized by abnormal or disturbed eating habits, including Anorexia Nervosa, Bulimia Nervosa, and Binge Eating Disorder.
 
• **Body Dysmorphic Disorder:** A mental health condition where a person spends a lot of time worrying about flaws in their appearance, which are often unnoticeable to others.
 
• **DSM-5 Criteria:** The Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition, outlines specific criteria for diagnosing Anorexia Nervosa, including restriction of energy intake relative to requirements, intense fear of gaining weight, and disturbance in the way one's body weight or shape is experienced.
 
• **Health Risks:** Anorexia Nervosa can lead to severe physical health issues, such as electrolyte imbalances, cardiovascular complications, osteoporosis, and amenorrhea.
 
• **Treatment Options:** Include psychotherapy, nutritional counseling, medical monitoring, and sometimes medications to address underlying mental health issues.

questions.question: Crocodiles have a ______ chambered heart.
questions.solution:
**Crocodiles** have a **__four-chambered__ heart.**

 
• Adaptation to their maximum portion of the life cycle is done in water since they need to minimize the oxygen loss when submerged and the **four-chambered hearts decrease the heartbeat by 2-3/minute** and normalize this rate when the crocodile is above water.
 
• The crocodile may have the **most complex circulatory vertebrate system. **
 
• This has a four-chambered heart and two ventricles, an uncommon characteristic between the current reptiles, and both the left and the right aorta, which are connected by a hole called the **Panizza Foramen.**
 
• Crocodiles belong to **Crocodylidae family.**
